method: The stylus rides a circle of radius r around the spindle while the arm pivots a distance d away, so with an effective length L the angle at the stylus between the arm and the radius is beta, where cos(beta) = (r^2 + L^2 - d^2) / (2 r L). The cartridge is tangent only when beta = 90 - offset, so the null radii solve r^2 - 2 L sin(offset) r + (L^2 - d^2) = 0 and their product is always L^2 - d^2: nulls = L sin(offset) +/- sqrt(L^2 sin^2(offset) - (L^2 - d^2)). Tracking error is offset - (90 - beta) in degrees: zero at both nulls, positive between them where the fixed offset exceeds what the groove needs, negative outside them, and its positive peak sits at sqrt(L^2 - d^2). The smallest offset that reaches a null anywhere is asin(sqrt(L^2 - d^2) / L), which is refused below rather than reported as zero error; overhang is L - d. The default 230 mm arm mounted 211.5 mm from the spindle at 23.5 degrees has 18.5 mm of overhang, nulls at 76.11 and 107.31 mm, -1.68 degrees at the 60.325 mm inner groove, -2.54 degrees at the 146.05 mm outer edge and a 0.36 degree peak at 90.38 mm, so its worst error is 2.54 degrees at the outer edge. The model is static geometry only: the arm is taken as straight, the stylus exactly at the effective length and the offset angle as stated; stylus shape, wear, anti-skate, VTA and record eccentricity are not modelled and no listening judgement is implied.

sources.title: A pivoted tonearm is tangent to a groove only at two radii; their product is the arm's effective length squared minus its mounting distance squared.
Tracking error is the angle between the cantilever and the groove tangent, signed positive when the cantilever toes toward the record edge.
